This surah is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

{1–2} He, the Exalted, says, explaining what will happen on the Day of Resurrection to the great celestial bodies of change: {When the sky is split open}; that is, it will be cleaved, and its parts will separate from one another, its stars will be scattered, and its sun and moon will be darkened. {And it listens to its Lord}; that is, it hearkens to His command, gives ear, and attends to His address. In other words, it is right that it should do so, for it is subjugated and governed under the control of a Mighty King whose command is not disobeyed and whose judgment is not opposed.

{3–5} {And when the earth is stretched out}; that is, it will quake and tremble, its mountains will be blown away over it, and whatever buildings and landmarks are upon it will be leveled and flattened. Allah will stretch it like a leather hide until it becomes exceedingly vast, large enough to hold the people of the gathering despite their multitude, so that it becomes a level plain in which you see no crookedness or elevation. {And it casts out what is within it}: the dead and the treasures. {And it empties itself}: of them. For the Trumpet will be blown, the dead will come out of their graves onto the surface of the earth, and the earth will bring forth its treasures until it becomes like a great pillar, which creation witnesses while lamenting over what they were competing for in this world. {And it listens to its Lord and is right to do so.}

{6} {O mankind, indeed you are laboring toward your Lord with labor and will meet Him}; that is, you are striving toward Allah, acting upon His commands and prohibitions, and drawing near to Him, either through good or through evil. Then you will meet Allah on the Day of Resurrection, and you will not lack a recompense from Him, whether by bounty or by justice: by bounty if you are among the happy, and by punishment if you are among the wretched.

{7–9} For this reason He mentions the detailed recompense, saying: {As for he who is given his record in his right hand}: and they are the people of happiness, {he will be reckoned with an easy account}: which is a light presentation before Allah, whereby Allah will make him acknowledge his sins, until, when the servant thinks he has perished, Allah the Exalted will say: "Indeed I concealed them for you in the world, and I conceal them for you today." {And he will return to his family}: in Paradise, {joyful}: because he has been saved from punishment and has succeeded in reward.

{10–15} {But as for he who is given his record behind his back}; that is, with his left hand from behind his back, {he will call for destruction}: from disgrace and humiliation, and from what he finds in his record of deeds he committed and did not repent of. {And he will burn in a Blaze}; that is, the Blaze will surround him from every side, and he will be turned over in its punishment. This is because he {used to be joyful among his people}: not contemplating the Resurrection, though he did wrong, and not thinking that he would return to his Lord and be made to stand before Him. {Yes! Indeed his Lord was ever Seeing of him}: so it is not fitting that He leave him neglected, neither commanded nor forbidden, neither rewarded nor punished.

This surah is Meccan.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 84, verses 16–25:

{16–19} In this place He swears by the signs of the night. He swears by al-shafaq (the twilight), which is the remnant of the sun's light and the beginning of the night, and by {the night and what it gathers}; that is, what it encompasses of living creatures and other things; and by {the moon when it becomes full}; that is, it becomes full of light when it is at its full phase, and that is the finest state it can be in and the most beneficial. The matter sworn to is His saying: {You will surely embark}; that is, O people, {stage after stage}; that is, through various stages and differing conditions: from the sperm-drop to the clot, to the lump of flesh, to the breathing of the spirit, then he becomes an infant, then a child, then one who discerns; then the pen of obligation, command and prohibition runs over him; then he dies after that; then he is resurrected and recompensed for his deeds. These successive stages that pass over the servant indicate that Allah alone is the one worthy of worship, the sole Lord who manages His servants with His wisdom and mercy, and that the servant is poor and powerless under the management of the All-Mighty, the All-Merciful.

{20–24} Despite this, many people do not believe. {And when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate}; that is, they do not submit to the Qur'an nor yield to its commands and prohibitions. {Rather, those who disbelieve deny}; that is, they obstinately oppose the truth after it has become clear. So their failure to believe and submit to the Qur'an is not strange, for one who denies the truth out of obstinacy has no remedy. {And Allah knows best what they conceal}; that is, what they do and intend in secret. Allah knows their secret and their open affairs, and He will recompense them for their deeds. For this reason He said: {So give them the tidings of a painful punishment}. The word bushra (tidings) was so named because it affects the skin (bashra) with joy or sorrow.

{25} This is the condition of most people: denial of the Qur'an and failure to believe in it. Among people, however, is a group whom Allah has guided, so they believed in Allah and accepted what the messengers brought. {Those who believe and do righteous deeds}: for them is {a reward never cut off}; that is, not interrupted, but a lasting reward of that which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and which has not occurred to the heart of any human being. And praise be to Allah.
